Front-expiry (11-13) straddle 14.21%, event-implied 13.58%. 25-delta put skew is +14.6 vol points ('downside paid'), but put/call OI is 0.29 (sealed baseline, Yahoo options, 2026-11-10). The last four prints moved -21.0%, -12.4%, +13.7% and -10.1% (median absolute 13.0%, 1 of 4 up). The stock ran from $5.78 (10-30) to $6.59 (11-04), then fell 15% into the print: -4.7% on 11-09 and -4.1% on 11-10, after Live Nation (11-05) and Vivid Seats (11-09) reported (Yahoo daily bars). Consensus per an Earnings Whispers preview dated 2026-11-03: Q3 revenue $529.8M (+13% y/y on $468.1M) and EPS $0.11. Aggregators show $524-528M. I found no published GMS or EBITDA consensus. The FY2026 guide was set 2026-08-12: GMS $10.1-10.3B (raised from $9.9-10.1B) and adj. EBITDA $400-420M (held). StubHub guides annually only. Short interest is about 31.2M shares at 2026-09-30, roughly 8% of the ~382M shares outstanding, 3.7 days to cover. Bearish sentiment readings rose to 41.7% from 12% a quarter earlier (Earnings Whispers). BofA is at Underperform with a $7.50 target, Guggenheim Neutral $7.50, and Citi upgraded 2026-09-18 on app downloads, expecting a Q3 EBITDA beat.
view: This print turns on two things. (1) Does Q3 GMS and revenue meet a consensus that implies roughly 9-12% Q3 GMS growth? (My arithmetic: $529.8M at a 19.2-19.9% take rate needs $2.66-2.76B of GMS against $2.43B a year ago.) The industry was flat in the same quarter: Ticketmaster resale GTV was flat, with concert resale down on its anti-scalping measures, and Vivid Seats GOV was +1%. July World Cup knockout resale sits in Q3, and StubHub has taken share all year, so a high-single-digit to low-double-digit Q3 is plausible and not a clear miss. (2) Does the FY guide hold? The GMS range implies only +0.5% to +4.8% H2 GMS growth, and with a strong Q3 that means a flat-to-down Q4. The EBITDA range needs $222-242M in H2 against $130M a year earlier (+71% to +86%), an H2 EBITDA margin of about 23-25% of revenue against 16-18% in H1. That is a steep ramp. Management said on the Q2 call that it expects H2 margin expansion as World Cup costs fade, and Citi (Sept) expects a Q3 EBITDA beat. A trim to the low end, or a cut, would be the bear catalyst. Reiteration at about 7-8x EV/EBITDA, with bearish sentiment high and the stock near its lows, would be the bull case. The 2027 risks are an MLB lockout (CBA expires 2026-12-01 and a stoppage is widely expected), state resale caps (Maine, Vermont, the Massachusetts proposal) and Live Nation restricting concert resale. They are all public and discussed, and StubHub gives annual guidance in its Q4 print, so 2027 color is likely limited tonight. The stock's history is down on 3 of 4 prints on credibility problems, and the options already pay for downside. I find no dated datapoint since August that the price clearly does not hold: the industry read-throughs came out in the last five sessions and the stock fell about 15% on them. Direction is close to a coin flip, with a slight lean down on the H2 margin ramp and the print history, and a large move either way.

recommendation.reason: The decisive lines are Q3 GMS against a consensus implying about 10% growth and whether the steep H2 EBITDA ramp ($222-242M against $130M a year ago) is reiterated. The public evidence does not settle either. The industry read-through (Ticketmaster resale flat, Vivid +1%) is negative for growth but was published in the last five sessions and the stock fell about 15% on it. Valuation and sentiment argue for a relief rally if the guide holds. I cannot show that the price is behind on either side.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A cut or trim of the FY2026 adj. EBITDA range below $400M, or Q3 GMS growth in low single digits (well under the ~10% the revenue consensus implies), would make a down move likely. Q3 adj. EBITDA above ~$110M with the guide reiterated would make an up move likely.

self_critique: The case for a lean down: the H2 EBITDA ramp is steep, the industry was flat in Q3, the revenue consensus needs about 10% GMS growth, and this management has disappointed on 3 of 4 prints. The case for up: the stock is at about 7-8x guided EBITDA with ~$600M of trailing FCF, sentiment is washed out, even the bears' targets ($7.50) sit 33% above spot, Citi expects a Q3 EBITDA beat, and the pre-print fall already took in the read-throughs. A reiterated guide could squeeze a market about 8% short. The two cases roughly offset, which is why I stay near 50 and make no recommendation.
approach_notes: P4 (priced-in is a claim to prove) helped: the Live Nation and Vivid read-throughs looked like a short case until the tape showed a 15% fall after them. P3's 'freshest data' route was thin here, with no alt-data series reachable publicly, so the view rests on guide arithmetic and peer prints.
